_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.354 (Default) with firmware rev27v-followup-338 (unchanged from v3.1.353).

System ID: a run started a few minutes after a preset no longer refuses its HIGH probes; the GUI keeps the controller's occlusion-exposure bound from every telemetry frame, so vented time counts as recovery (the safety limit is unchanged). A fast but smooth valve-open probe is measured when quiet readings around it rule out pulses. A pump overshoot above a probe's unchanged comparison window is removed with a short, measured partial-valve bleed followed by a fresh sealed reading. System ID and Cal 2/Cal 4 archives are filed under the connected device. On Device D (wrist cuff on syringe) a compare-only System ID now completes all three bands; its quality checks still decide whether a result is acceptable.

Stability: after the window has shut down in order, Smart Cuff ends without Python/Qt teardown, removing an intermittent crash at close.

Also: the deflation heart-rate estimate survives the short telemetry pause after Smart Const's MAP analysis; the live plot time axis no longer shows a scale suffix while the first samples arrive.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
